claim_boundary: A fall in the New York Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index can reflect easing logistics and input bottlenecks, weaker goods demand, changing transportation costs, manufacturing-survey conditions or data revisions. Exactly one future preregistered long-or-cash audit may test whether the conservatively delayed three-month direction has matched-capital BTC value; no causal or alpha claim is imported from the sources.

primary_sources.identity: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Global Supply Chain Pressure Index
primary_sources.evidence: The New York Fed publishes the monthly GSCPI and an official downloadable workbook.
primary_sources.boundary: The current workbook is a present-vintage research product and does not establish unrevised real-time historical vintages or future Bitcoin returns.

primary_sources.identity: Federal Reserve Bank of New York GSCPI launch announcement
primary_sources.evidence: The index integrates transportation-cost data and manufacturing indicators and is scheduled for 10:00 ET on the fourth business day of each month.
primary_sources.boundary: A regular release schedule supports a conservative availability lag but does not remove revisions or guarantee tradable publication latency.

primary_sources.identity: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 1017
primary_sources.evidence: The paper defines the GSCPI as a common global supply-chain component built from transportation and manufacturing variables and studies its relation to inflation.
primary_sources.boundary: The paper does not test Bitcoin timing, and lower supply-chain pressure may arise from weaker demand rather than benign normalization.

adversarial_prior: Lower supply-chain pressure can be caused by falling goods demand or recession risk rather than healthier productive capacity.
The index combines many inputs and can change when source histories or model estimates are revised.
Its inflation channel can overlap with already closed inflation and financial-conditions families without adding independent BTC timing value.
A monthly composite may react too slowly to preserve BTC upside or avoid fast drawdown paths.
prohibited_rescue: Do not add component shipping rates, manufacturing surveys, CPI, PPI, commodities, the dollar, equities, rates, BTC trend, volatility or on-chain inputs.
Do not change the three-month horizon, easing direction, 45-day availability floor, threshold, sizing or parent after source or outcome access.
Do not reinterpret closed CPI-disinflation, financial-conditions, oil, copper or macro-activity families as support for this one.

independence.distinct_from_closed_inflation: The decision input is an upstream common component of transportation and manufacturing conditions, not a consumer-price level or release-day event.
independence.distinct_from_closed_commodities: The decision input is a multi-source supply-chain pressure index, not the direction of copper, crude oil or another single commodity price.
independence.distinct_from_closed_financial_condition: The input is designed to measure physical supply-chain pressures, not credit spreads, market volatility or a broad financial-conditions index.
